data.long_meaning: From the Greek word ‘Thaddaios’ which means ‘little one’ or ‘gift of God’. In the Bible, Thaddaeus, also known as Judas Iscariot, was one of the twelve apostles of Jesus. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Thaddaeus usually hope their child will grow to embody gift of god and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_hebrew.name: תדאיוס
in_hebrew.meaning: לב טוב ולב חזק לתת ולחזק
in_hebrew.long_meaning: תדאיוס הוא שם שמשמעותו 'לב טוב' או 'לב חזק', ומקורו בשפה הארמית. השם תדאיוס מורכב משתי מילים: 'תדא' שפירושה 'לב' ו- 'יוס' שפירושה 'טוב' או 'חזק'. השם נמצא בברית החדשה ומתייחס לאחד מתלמידיו של ישוע, תדאיוס הקדוש.

in_greek.name: Θαδδαῖος
in_greek.long_meaning: Θαδδαῖος (Θαδδαῖος) προέρχεται από την αρamaϊκή γλώσσα και σημαίνει 'καρδία ἀγαθὴ' ἢ 'καρδία ἰσχυρά'. Ὁ ὄνομα Θαδδαῖος ἀναφέρεται στὴν Καινή Διαθήκη καὶ συγκεκριμένα στὸ Εὐαγγέλιο τοῦ Ματθαίου (Ματθ. 10:3) καὶ στὴν Πράξεις τῶν Αποστόλων (Πρξ. 1:13). Ὁ Θαδδαῖος ἦταν ἕνας τῶν δώδεκα ἀποστόλων τοῦ Ιησού Χριστού.

in_latin.name: Thaddaeus
in_latin.long_meaning: Thaddaeus nomen derivatum est ex lingua aramaica, significans 'bonus cor' seu 'cor robustum'. Nomen Thaddaeus in Novo Testamento invenitur et quidem in Evangelio Matthaei (Mt 10,3) et in Actibus Apostolorum (Act 1,13). Thaddaeus fuit unus de duodecim apostolis Iesu Christi.

in_english.name: Thaddaeus
in_english.long_meaning: Thaddaeus is a Christian name derived from the Aramaic language, meaning 'heart', 'courageous', or 'praised'. The name Thaddaeus originates from the Hebrew and Greek roots, specifically from the Aramaic name 'Thadde', which means 'heart' and the Greek suffix '-eus', which signifies a place or a person. Thaddaeus was one of the twelve apostles of Jesus Christ, mentioned in the New Testament, specifically in the Gospel of Matthew (Mt 10:3) and in the Acts of the Apostles (Acts 1:13). The name Thaddaeus has been used in various Christian cultures and traditions, symbolizing spiritual courage and devotion.
